v%1$s · all data stays on this phone

It moves your phone contacts, messages and call history into an encrypted local vault: every record is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it hits the disk, so the database holds no readable names, numbers or message bodies. Paired with the caller ID overlay, even an unknown number shows you who it is.

Fixed dual-SIM messages that could not be deleted while the counter showed 0: incoming messages now carry the SIM subscription id, deletion goes message by message to bypass the system subscription filter, and results break down what is left by SIM
Clearing system messages now covers MMS too; the system count includes both SMS and MMS, results break down deleted and remaining by type, and the parts that need manual deletion are spelled out

Prominent reminder to switch back from the default SMS role after restoring or clearing; restored the ability to delete system call logs, and system messages / call logs can be selected again when clearing
Fixed two missing declarations that kept this app out of the default SMS app list; Restore data can now check eligibility
Copy your system contacts in all at once; after clearing the system you can write them back any time from Restore data, and before uninstalling remember to restore or export a CSV
The key is generated by the system Keystore, never written to disk and never exportable — even if the database is copied away, its contents stay unreadable

Text messages are encrypted as a whole and can be read and exported to CSV; writing back or clearing system messages requires this app to become the default SMS app first - switch back to your usual app afterwards. MMS bodies are not stored
Call history is kept encrypted, so numbers and durations never land in plain text — always available to search and export; the system records can be cleared, but cannot be written back
Shows the caller\'s name in an overlay on incoming calls — identification only, no blocking, no recording, no uploading
No account, no server, no analytics — all data lives on this phone only

Every permission is required by the feature it belongs to, and each one is requested only when you open that feature — nothing is demanded all at once at startup:
· Contacts (read) — import your system contacts into the encrypted vault · Contacts (write) — only needed in Restore data to write the vault back to the system · SMS (read) — import your system messages into the encrypted vault · SMS (write) — since Android 4.4 only the default SMS app may write to the message store, so switching the default SMS app once is required before restoring messages · SMS / MMS receive — declared in the manifest only so the system recognises this app as a default SMS candidate; this app never requests them and does not receive messages during normal use · Call log (read) — import your system call history into the encrypted vault · Phone state — dismiss the caller ID overlay after the call ends · Overlay / notifications — show the caller ID card and the ongoing notification
There is no network permission, and no location, camera, microphone, or storage permission.
MIT licensed — feel free to build, modify, and redistribute it. The source contains no backend at all; every feature runs on your phone.

· Duplicate contacts are tagged as "Duplicate" automatically after an import, and you can re-run Check duplicates on the contacts backup page; search the number to locate them
· Uninstalling also wipes the encryption key — before that, write the data back from Restore data or export a CSV
· SMS and call history need their own permissions, and are stored encrypted on this device only
· The system does not allow writing call history back to the phone call log, so it can only be read and exported here
· The caller ID overlay needs the "display over other apps" permission; some Chinese ROMs also require allowing pop-ups in the background

Every deletion of messages, call history and contacts is collected here. Pick which copy to clear first, then select the contents, then type the confirmation word.

Delete the original data in the phone system apps and keep this app\'s encrypted copy. Messages need this app to be the default SMS app, and call logs need the write call log permission; if a requirement is missing you will be prompted to grant it first
Only delete the encrypted copies stored here; the originals in your phone are not affected
That confirmation word is not right \u2014 type \"%1$s\"
Tick at least one thing to clear

· Clearing cannot be undone, make sure you exported a CSV backup · Contacts stored in a cloud account may sync the deletion to the cloud · Clearing system messages wipes every text message and MMS on the phone, including ones you just restored · MMS bodies are not in the encrypted vault and cannot be recovered after deletion - save them elsewhere first · Messages received after clearing are not deleted retroactively; messages on another SIM, SIM-card storage, and RCS / service card messages may be invisible to this app and need manual deletion in your messaging app · Clearing system messages needs the default SMS app role; clearing system call logs needs WRITE_CALL_LOG. Some ROMs refuse, and any failure is reported honestly · Clearing this app\'s encrypted copy is not restricted by the system, all three work
Needs this app to be the default SMS app. Both text messages and MMS are cleared; switch back to your usual messaging app when you are done
Needs the write call log permission. The remaining count is read back afterwards, and any failure is reported
Default SMS app is still needed

Since Android 4.4 only the default SMS app may delete system messages. Use the button to set this app as the default SMS app, then switch back to your usual messaging app when you are done - the role does not revert on its own.
Call log write permission is still needed
Deleting system call logs needs the WRITE_CALL_LOG permission. It is a normal runtime permission; some vendor ROMs refuse it, and the result will say so.

If your messaging app still shows messages, they may be on another SIM / in SIM-card storage, RCS or service card messages in a vendor-private store, or messages received after the clear (those are not deleted retroactively). Delete those manually in your messaging app. Since v1.8.4 incoming messages carry the SIM subscription id and deletion is done message by message; run one more clear to remove older untagged messages.
If the contacts come from a cloud account, deleting them may sync back to the cloud.

This role does not revert after a few minutes, and Android does not let an app hand it back - you have to switch manually. Incoming text messages are written back into the system message store (so their content is not lost), but this app shows no new-message notification and MMS may not arrive. Write the contents of the encrypted vault back into the phone system. Useful if you changed your mind after clearing, or when switching phones. Existing content is compared first and skipped, so no duplicate contacts or messages are created. Call logs can be deleted but not written back (the CallLog provider rejects inserts), so that option is not offered here.

Writing contacts back into the system needs the WRITE_CONTACTS permission. Grant it and the restore will go through.
Default SMS app is still needed

Since Android 4.4 only the default SMS app may write to the system message store. When this app is not the default one, the system accepts the write request without actually writing anything, and the messages never show up in your messaging app. Use the button to set this app as the default SMS app, then switch back to your usual messaging app when you are done.
Not listed as a default SMS app?
Android filters default SMS candidates by four fixed checks. Run the check to see whether a declaration is missing or the phone maker blocks it.

All four declarations are present, so Android should list this app as a candidate. If Settings - Default apps - SMS still does not show it, the phone maker is likely whitelisting default SMS apps, which code cannot bypass. In that case messages cannot be written back; export a CSV instead.
